findings.description: The repair overshot in the opposite direction and opened a new seam: the text still requires that each new scratch path appear in a trap carrying "every path from the trap before it", but the check now inspects only "the last `EXIT` trap the job adds", so a job adding four traps where the second drops a path from the first and the third silently restores it satisfies the check and violates the text — the same leak-on-early-exit shape as #30, which the text forbids and the check can no longer see.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:133 text ('each new scratch path appears in an `EXIT` trap that also carries every path from the trap before it') vs. constitution.md:134 check ('confirm that the last `EXIT` trap the job adds carries every path from the trap immediately preceding it, plus every scratch path the job itself creates'). Repair: have the check walk every trap the job adds against the trap immediately before it, not only the last.

findings.description: The new grep bullet reaches the right conclusion from a wrong mechanism and names the wrong remedy: the instability is not environmental, it is a `grep` shell function Claude Code installs in the agent's interactive snapshot that execs `ugrep 7.5.0`, and it does not exist inside any `bash script.sh` invocation, where `grep` is `/usr/bin/grep` (BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD) and is stable — so `lint-scope.sh` and the smoke suite were never exposed, and `rtk proxy grep` is stable because it bypasses the wrapper to the real grep rather than because rtk stabilizes anything.
findings.evidence: `type grep` in the agent shell resolves to a function from /Users/karnett/.claude/shell-snapshots/snapshot-zsh-*.sh that runs `ARGV0=ugrep "$_cc_bin" -G ...`; `grep --version` there reports 'ugrep 7.5.0'. Same selector run 10x in the agent shell: 6x 2026-01-27-atlas-freeze-check, 4x 2026-02-03-atlas-dry-run-prep. The identical loop inside a bash script reports `/usr/bin/grep`, 'grep (BSD grep, GNU compatible) 2.6.0-FreeBSD', and returns 2026-01-27-atlas-freeze-check 10 times out of 10.

findings.description: The bullet's operative conclusion is nonetheless correct and I confirmed it two independent ways, so only the explanation needs rewriting, not the directive it carries: nothing in `lint-scope.sh` depends on grep ordering, and C-4 cannot flap.
findings.evidence: Every multi-match grep in lint-scope.sh is either piped to `sort -u` (:230, :379, :430, :461) or is a membership/count test whose result is order-free (:193, :227, :243, :250-251, :278, :296, :315, :328, :332, :348, :375, :377, :454, :459); the three `head -1` sites (:184, :234, :357) read a single stream. Empirically: lint output on `mixed` is one sha across 12 runs; C-4's full check printed 'diff=0' on 6 consecutive runs. C-4 is order-proof by construction anyway — its own `grep -E … | sort` normalizes before `diff`.

findings.description: The repaired fail trigger closes the round-0 hole but leaves a deletion loophole: the check fails a location when the named line makes its sentence false or when no line can be tied to it, and a worker who deletes the v1 paragraph at `:10-12` outright rather than correcting it leaves no sentence to quote, making the location vacuously compliant while the file loses the contract statement the clause exists to keep honest.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:140-141. The text's premise ('Four locations state which checks a v1 file receives') implies the statement must survive, but nothing in the check says so. Repair: add that each location must still state which checks a v1 file receives — removing the claim is not a repair of it.

findings.description: PASS, and the two-command check does jointly cover the two-claim text with no third mode escaping, though for a reason worth recording: the injection in check one triggers only four of the nine named checks directly, and the other five are covered transitively because the six body-grammar checks sit in one atomic `if ! has_v1_body` block, so firing any of them fires `check_tokens`, which the injection does catch.
findings.evidence: lint-scope.sh:444-451 is a single guarded block; check_tensions (:283), check_contradictions (:324), check_decisions (:337) cannot run without check_tokens (:445) running too. The RECURRING half of the text needs no separate check because RECURRING and the resolution loop read the same file: lint-scope.sh:472-476 `sort "$work/open-slugs" | uniq -c` and lint-scope.sh:459 `grep -Fqx -- "$slug" "$work/open-slugs"`. Optional hardening only: adding `[tension: …]`, `[contradicts accepted: …]`, and `[decision: …]` to the injected block would make the coverage direct rather than transitive.

findings.description: PASS on discrimination, verified by simulation: the new second check prints the required line against the stock tree and against a simulated correct fix, and goes silent against the slug-harvest widening it was written to catch, which is the exact behavior the round-0 diagnosis asked for.
findings.evidence: Stock: 'FAIL …/2026-01-27-atlas-freeze-check-o7fhuG__gc.md: open-question-resolution: `v1-only-slug` is resolved here but never opened anywhere in scope' / 'failures: 2'. Simulated correct fix: same line, 'failures: 2'. Simulated harvest widening: line absent, 'failures: 1'. Note selection via `ls`-ordered awk classification was stable across runs (V1=2025-12-02-atlas-steerco, V2=2026-01-27-atlas-freeze-check), and both `mixed` v1 notes carry the `## Raw Content` fence the inject helper seeks.

findings.description: PASS: dropping the humanizer from the clause text is the right call given checker-judgment has no Skill tool, and text and check now name the same three testable properties, with the typographic rules scoped to rewritten passages only so no pre-existing prose makes the clause unsatisfiable.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:154 text (reason alongside rule; no bolded inline header with a colon; em dashes chained rather than space-wrapped) matched one-for-one by constitution.md:155 check. The `humanizer` skill exists at ~/.claude/skills/humanizer, so moving the obligation to the executing worker's task keeps it enforceable by whoever can actually run it.
